mil1:1.1: Homage to that Blessed One, the Perfected One, the Fully Awakened Buddha.
mil1:7.2: There is a city of the Greeks named Sāgala, where bales of goods of many kinds are opened; adorned with rivers and mountains, with delightful tracts of land, rich in parks, pleasure gardens, woods, lakes, and lotus ponds, lovely with rivers, mountains, and forests; built by learned people, with enemies destroyed, not oppressed by hostile foes; with strong watchtowers and gatehouses of many varied kinds, with excellent and splendid gates and archways; its inner city surrounded by a deep moat and a white rampart.
mil1:7.3: Its streets, squares, crossroads, and junctions are well divided; its shops in the middle are well spread out and filled with many kinds of excellent goods; it is adorned with hundreds of kinds of almshalls, and decked with hundreds of thousands of excellent mansions that look like peaks of the Himalaya; it is crowded with elephants, horses, chariots, and infantry; frequented by throngs of beautiful men and women; thronged with people; full of many aristocrats, brahmins, merchants, and workers; filled with the hospitality shown to ascetics and brahmins of many kinds; long frequented by people of many branches of knowledge; rich in shops with many kinds of cloth, such as Kāsian and Koṭumbara cloth; with well-spread, lovely shops selling many kinds of flowers and perfumes, fragrant with scent; filled with many desirable jewels; with shops well spread out toward every direction; frequented by throngs of merchants of ornaments; full of kahāpaṇa coins, silver, gold, bronze, and stone; with shining treasure-houses; abundant in wealth, grain, property, and equipment; with full treasuries and granaries; with abundant food and drink, and many kinds of things to chew, eat, lick, drink, and savor; like Uttarakuru, with excellent crops; like Āḷakamandā, the city of the gods.
mil1:8.1: Pausing here, their former deeds should be told; and one who tells them should divide the telling into six parts.
mil1:8.3: the past practice, the questions of Milinda, the questions on characteristics, the questions of Meṇḍaka, the questions by inference, and the questions by similes.
mil1:9.1: Among them, the questions of Milinda are of two kinds: the questions on characteristics, and the questions that cut off doubt.
mil1:9.2: The questions of Meṇḍaka are also of two kinds: the Great Chapter, and the questions on the account of the yogis.
